title: add-playbook-sampler-cli-and-runtime-validation
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Add 'sloctl sample-playbook' to generate minimal incident playbooks and validate them against SLO definitions. Includes CLI docs and unit tests.
description: This PR introduces a lightweight playbook sampler that generates candidate incident playbooks from live SLOs, recent error-rate slices, and alert fingerprints. The goal is to help oncall engineers rapidly assemble a minimal, actionable playbook when a new alert fires or when creating runbook templates for new services. The sampler includes: a CLI command 'sloctl sample-playbook' with flags for lookback window and severity heuristics, a runtime validator that checks playbook steps against available runbooks and telemetry queries, Slack-formatted snippet output for quick pasting, and end-to-end unit tests and integration smoke checks. Motivation: incidents often start with a blank template or outdated runbooks. By surfacing an evidence-backed starter playbook and validating actions against available traces/metrics, we reduce time-to-first-action and misdirected escalations. This change touches the core toolkit CLI and adds a small runtime library with no external service dependencies. Backwards compatibility: no existing commands are removed. Usage example: 'sloctl sample-playbook --service billing --lookback=30m --severity=high --output=slack' produces a 3-5 step playbook with diagnostics queries, quick mitigations, and suggested assignees.

review_comments: Rahul Patel: Nice surface area reduction, this will be useful for oncall. Two asks: 1) add a flag to pin an SLO revision when generating sample playbooks, and 2) ensure the Slack output obfuscates any PII in metric labels.

Maya Thompson: Thanks Rahul, added --slo-revision flag and a label-sanitizer step in output builder. See commit b3d2f11 and output_slack.go. Slack output now strips user ids unless '--include-labels' is provided by the operator in an interactive mode.

Lena Gomez: Validator is good but the current runtime query list is inline in code. Can we make it configurable and loadable from ~/.slo-toolkit/config.yaml? Also we need a short circuit when telemetry backend is unreachable to avoid blocking the CLI.

Maya Thompson: Agreed, updated validator to read optional config with default baked-in queries and added a 5s timeout/fallback that marks validation as 'skipped (telemetry unreachable)'. Commit d5f12b0 includes tests for the fallback behavior.
Ethan Cole: Tests look solid. Nit: add a small table-driven test for severity heuristics covering high/medium/low transitions. Also CI failed once on lint; can you run 'gofmt' and re-run?
Maya Thompson: Added table-driven tests and ran gofmt. CI lint failure was due to a trailing whitespace in docs; fixed in e6a77c3. Rerun CI passed.
discussion_summary: Reviewers asked for configurability, telemetry timeout behavior, and PII handling in outputs. Author added --slo-revision, config-backed validator defaults, telemetry fallback, and label sanitizer. Tests and docs were added. Final approvals granted after fixes.
